source_refs.note: Topic 9.3.2 with the Did You Know (PDF 213-214, printed 210-211). Long question 3 is answered.

items: Trends and patterns: a survey shows most bakery purchases happen at weekends, so focus promotions on weekends.
Segmenting the market: split customers by age, income or habits; younger customers prefer sweet pastries, older ones whole-grain bread.
Competitor analysis: study rivals' strengths, prices and feedback; if a nearby bakery is known for artisanal bread, offer gourmet pastries or seasonal cakes.
Predictive analysis: use past data to forecast; steadily rising demand suggests increasing production.
Data-driven decisions: choose products, prices and marketing from the data; drop an underperforming product.

blocks.text: Digital platforms have also changed education; adaptive learning platforms adjust lesson difficulty to each student's progress (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: How does market insight influence business decisions? Give examples (long question 3).
blocks.explanation: It replaces guesswork with evidence. Trends decide timing (weekend promotions); segmentation shapes products and messages (sweet pastries for the young, whole-grain bread for older buyers); competitor analysis shows how to stand out (gourmet pastries beside a rival's artisanal bread); prediction guides production; and poor sales data can justify dropping a product. Surveys of price tolerance set prices.

items: Analyse data for trends, segments, competitors and predictions; then decide.
